title: 🔑 Farhan reused one password... the breach that opens five accounts #passwords #cybersecurity
title_alts: 🗝 Farhan's password manager story... one vault instead of five keys #passwords #cybersecurity
🚨 Farhan almost reused his email password... stop credential stuffing #passwords #cybersecurity
description_hook: One leaked password only hurts if you used it twice. Here is how credential stuffing turns a stranger's breach into your locked-out morning.
setting: a home desk, a warehouse of leaked records, and a corridor of identical doors
protagonist_type: an office worker who manages his own logins

characters.name: Farhan
characters.description: twenty-nine, short black hair, navy zip-up fleece, a lanyard with three old office badges still on it

claims.claim: One stolen password can unlock five of your accounts.
claims.basis: round illustrative count of reused logins, offered as an example rather than a measurement
illustrative order of magnitude for a leaked credential dump, stated as a rough scale

claims.claim: Say one password guards eight of your logins.
claims.basis: round illustrative assumption, introduced in the narration with the word say
arithmetic that follows directly from the eight reused logins just stated

claims.claim: A password manager stores eight different secrets.
claims.basis: follows from the same eight logins, one distinct secret for each

claims.claim: One breach now costs one account.
claims.basis: follows from each login holding its own distinct secret

scenes.narration: One stolen password can unlock five of your accounts.
scenes.caption: एक चोरी हुआ पासवर्ड आपके पाँच अकाउंट खोल सकता है
scenes.image_brief: A single brass key lying on a dark wooden desk beside five closed padlocks arranged in a row, warm lamp light from the left, the rest of the desk in shadow.

scenes.narration: Attackers buy leaked email and password pairs in bulk. Millions per file.
scenes.caption: हैकर लीक हुई ईमेल-पासवर्ड जोड़ियाँ थोक में खरीदते हैं, एक फ़ाइल में लाखों
scenes.image_brief: A cardboard box on a metal warehouse shelf overflowing with printed slips, each slip showing an email address and a row of dots, cold blue overhead light, more boxes receding down the aisle behind it.

scenes.narration: Then they replay them everywhere. Your bank included.
scenes.caption: फिर वे उन्हें हर जगह आज़माते हैं, आपके बैंक पर भी
scenes.image_brief: A long corridor of identical office doors with one door carrying a small bank nameplate, an identical key left in every lock along the row, dim light from a window at the far end.

scenes.narration: By the end you will know exactly which password to change first.
scenes.caption: अंत तक आप जान जाएंगे कि कौन सा पासवर्ड पहले बदलना है
scenes.image_brief: A small notepad on a kitchen table listing four account names in handwriting, the top line circled in red ink, soft morning light falling across the page.

scenes.narration: One site gets breached and your login pair leaks out.
scenes.caption: एक साइट हैक होती है और आपका लॉगिन जोड़ा लीक हो जाता है
scenes.image_brief: A server cabinet with one side panel hanging open and a crack across its frame, a thin stream of paper slips spilling from the gap onto the floor tiles, green indicator lights glowing inside the rack.

scenes.narration: Every site where you reused it opens. Nothing was guessed.
scenes.caption: जहाँ भी वही पासवर्ड लगाया, सब खुल गया, बिना कोई अंदाज़ा लगाए
scenes.image_brief: A wall of small metal mailbox doors with dozens of them swinging open at the same moment, no tools and no damage anywhere, flat fluorescent light from the ceiling.

scenes.narration: Say one password guards eight of your logins. One breach exposes eight.
scenes.caption: मान लीजिए एक पासवर्ड आठ लॉगिन संभालता है, एक लीक सब आठ खोल देती है
scenes.image_brief: Eight identical padlocks laid out in two neat rows on a white table with one single key resting in the centre between them, even daylight from a window above.

scenes.narration: A password manager stores eight different secrets. One breach now costs one account.
scenes.caption: पासवर्ड मैनेजर आठ अलग पासवर्ड रखता है, तो एक लीक से सिर्फ़ एक अकाउंट जाता है
scenes.image_brief: An open steel vault box on a desk holding eight differently shaped keys in separate labelled slots, every label showing a different website name, cool white light from directly above.

scenes.narration: This fails if your master password is short and reused too.
scenes.caption: यह काम नहीं करेगा अगर आपका मास्टर पासवर्ड छोटा और दोहराया हो
scenes.image_brief: A heavy bank vault door standing slightly ajar, held shut only by a tiny brass luggage padlock looped through its handle, low light raking across the steel.

scenes.narration: A notes file is not a manager. That file syncs unencrypted.
scenes.caption: नोट्स फ़ाइल मैनेजर नहीं है, वह बिना एन्क्रिप्शन सिंक होती है
scenes.image_brief: An open paper notebook page listing readable passwords in ink, lying face up on a glass table beside a switched-on wireless router with its lights lit, bright midday daylight.

scenes.narration: Reuse turns one company's breach into your personal problem. You cannot control their security.
scenes.caption: दोहराना किसी कंपनी की गलती को आपकी समस्या बना देता है
scenes.image_brief: A line of dominoes running from a distant office tower with one broken window, across a rooftop, and down to the front step of a small house, dusk with a low orange sky.

scenes.narration: End the reuse and the damage stays at that one site.
scenes.caption: दोहराना बंद करें और नुकसान उसी एक साइट तक सीमित रहेगा
scenes.image_brief: A cutaway apartment block where one single room is scorched black while every other room stays clean and furnished, warm even light across the whole face of the building.

scenes.narration: Change your email password tonight. Every reset link lands there.
scenes.caption: आज ही अपना ईमेल पासवर्ड बदलें, हर रीसेट लिंक वहीं आता है
scenes.image_brief: A laptop open on an evening desk showing an account security page with an empty new password field highlighted, warm lamp light spilling in from the left edge.

title: 🔒 Tanvi's two-factor codes arrive by text... the swap that steals them #2fa #cybersecurity
title_alts: 📲 Tanvi's authenticator app makes codes offline... no signal needed #2fa #cybersecurity
🚩 Tanvi moved her codes off text... the swap that empties accounts #2fa #cybersecurity
description_hook: Codes by text beat having no second step at all, and they are weaker than most people assume. Here is what a number transfer does to them.
problem_domain: two-factor authentication and phone number takeover
setting: a dark kitchen counter and a carrier service desk
protagonist_type: a freelancer who banks entirely from her phone

characters.name: Tanvi
characters.description: thirty-one, long dark hair in a single braid, olive green kurta, reading glasses pushed up on her head

claims.claim: It computes a six digit code on your phone.
claims.basis: standard authenticator code length, a long stable convention rather than a measured figure

claims.claim: The code changes every thirty seconds
claims.basis: standard time step used by authenticator apps, a stable convention rather than a measured figure

scenes.narration: A text message code protects less than you think.
scenes.caption: टेक्स्ट मैसेज से आने वाला कोड जितना लगता है, उतना बचाता नहीं
scenes.image_brief: A smartphone lying face up on a dark kitchen counter showing one open text message containing a six digit code, the screen the only light in the room.

scenes.narration: Your phone number can be moved to another phone. Phone numbers are portable.
scenes.caption: आपका फ़ोन नंबर दूसरे फ़ोन पर जा सकता है, नंबर पोर्टेबल होते हैं
scenes.image_brief: A small plastic phone card lying on a laminate service counter between two identical smartphones, the phone on the left dark and the phone on the right lit, cool overhead strip light.

scenes.narration: You will know which second factor survives that move.
scenes.caption: आप जान जाएंगे कि कौन सा दूसरा सुरक्षा कदम इस बदलाव में टिकता है
scenes.image_brief: Two objects side by side on a slate grey surface, a phone showing an incoming message bubble and a small keyring token showing two glowing digits, soft even light from above.

scenes.narration: Someone calls your carrier claiming your phone was lost or stolen.
scenes.caption: कोई आपके नेटवर्क ऑपरेटर को फ़ोन करके कहता है कि फ़ोन खो गया
scenes.image_brief: A telephone headset resting on a call centre desk beside a printed form with a lost handset box ticked in pen, flat fluorescent light, rows of empty desks behind it.

scenes.narration: Your number transfers. Every text code now arrives on their device.
scenes.caption: नंबर ट्रांसफ़र हो जाता है, हर टेक्स्ट कोड अब उनके फ़ोन पर आता है
scenes.image_brief: One smartphone on a bare table with message notifications stacked across its whole screen, while an identical smartphone across the table shows empty signal bars and nothing else, dim blue light.

scenes.narration: An authenticator app receives nothing. It computes a six digit code on your phone.
scenes.caption: ऑथेंटिकेटर एप कुछ नहीं लेता, वह छह अंकों का कोड फ़ोन में ही बनाता है
scenes.image_brief: A phone screen filled almost entirely by a single six digit code with a thin circular timer ring around it, the phone resting on a closed notebook, warm lamp light from above.

scenes.narration: The code changes every thirty seconds and never travels over the network.
scenes.caption: कोड हर तीस सेकंड में बदलता है और नेटवर्क पर कभी नहीं जाता
scenes.image_brief: The same phone screen a moment later showing a different six digit code with the circular timer ring almost empty, and a cut network cable lying beside the phone on the notebook.

scenes.narration: Text codes still beat no second factor at all.
scenes.caption: टेक्स्ट कोड फिर भी बिना किसी दूसरे कदम से बेहतर है
scenes.image_brief: A front door fitted with two locks, a solid deadbolt above and a thin chain latch below, both engaged, warm porch light on the paint.

scenes.narration: And no factor helps if you read the code aloud. Nobody legitimate asks.
scenes.caption: और कोई कदम काम नहीं आता अगर आप कोड बोल दें, असली कंपनी नहीं पूछती
scenes.image_brief: A phone lying on speaker on a desk beside a sticky note where a six digit code has been written out by hand, an unknown caller card showing on the screen, harsh overhead light.

scenes.narration: The strongest code is the one that never leaves your phone.
scenes.caption: सबसे मज़बूत कोड वही है जो आपके फ़ोन से बाहर कभी नहीं जाता
scenes.image_brief: A closed metal safe on a desk with a small glowing digit display set into its door and no cables or aerials attached anywhere, dim evening light from one side.

scenes.narration: Move your email account to an authenticator app first. Everything else recovers through it.
scenes.caption: पहले अपना ईमेल अकाउंट ऑथेंटिकेटर एप पर ले जाएं, बाकी सब उसी से मिलता है
scenes.image_brief: A phone propped against a coffee mug on a morning table showing an email account security page with an authenticator option switched on, bright daylight from a window.
